csf.name: NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0
csf.plain: A widely used checklist of outcomes for running a security program. Version 2.0 added a Govern section about leadership, roles, and risk decisions.

ids.GV.OC-01: Organizational mission is understood and informs cybersecurity risk management
ids.GV.OC-02: Internal and external stakeholders and their expectations are understood
ids.GV.OC-03: Legal, regulatory, and contractual requirements are understood and managed
ids.GV.OC-04: Critical objectives, capabilities, and services that stakeholders depend on are communicated
ids.GV.OC-05: Outcomes, capabilities, and services that the organization depends on are communicated
ids.GV.RM-01: Risk management objectives are established and agreed to by stakeholders
ids.GV.RM-02: Risk appetite and risk tolerance statements are established and communicated
ids.GV.RM-03: Cybersecurity risk management activities are included in enterprise risk management
ids.GV.RM-04: Strategic direction describing appropriate risk response options is established
ids.GV.RM-05: Lines of communication across the organization are established for cybersecurity risks
ids.GV.RM-06: A standardized method for calculating, documenting, categorizing, and prioritizing risks is established
ids.GV.RM-07: Strategic opportunities (positive risks) are characterized and included in discussions
ids.GV.RR-01: Leadership is responsible and accountable for cybersecurity risk and fosters a risk-aware culture
ids.GV.RR-02: Roles, responsibilities, and authorities related to cybersecurity risk management are established
ids.GV.RR-03: Adequate resources are allocated commensurate with the cybersecurity risk strategy
ids.GV.RR-04: Cybersecurity is included in human resources practices
ids.GV.PO-01: Policy for managing cybersecurity risks is established and communicated
ids.GV.PO-02: Policy for managing cybersecurity risks is reviewed, updated, communicated, and enforced
ids.GV.OV-01: Cybersecurity risk management strategy outcomes are reviewed to inform and adjust strategy
ids.GV.OV-02: The cybersecurity risk management strategy is reviewed and adjusted to ensure coverage
ids.GV.OV-03: Organizational cybersecurity risk management performance is evaluated and reviewed
ids.GV.SC-01: A cybersecurity supply chain risk management program is established and agreed to
ids.GV.SC-02: Cybersecurity roles and responsibilities for suppliers, customers, and partners are established
ids.GV.SC-03: Cybersecurity supply chain risk management is integrated into risk management and improvement
ids.GV.SC-04: Suppliers are known and prioritized by criticality
ids.GV.SC-05: Requirements to address cybersecurity risks in supply chains are established in contracts
ids.GV.SC-06: Planning and due diligence are performed to reduce risks before entering supplier relationships
ids.GV.SC-07: Supplier risks are understood, recorded, prioritized, assessed, responded to, and monitored
ids.GV.SC-08: Relevant suppliers and third parties are included in incident planning, response, and recovery
ids.GV.SC-09: Supply chain security practices are integrated into cybersecurity and ERM programs
ids.GV.SC-10: Cybersecurity supply chain risk management plans include provisions for the end of a relationship
ids.ID.AM-01: Inventories of hardware managed by the organization are maintained
ids.ID.AM-02: Inventories of software, services, and systems managed by the organization are maintained
ids.ID.AM-03: Representations of the organization's authorized network communication and data flows are maintained
ids.ID.AM-04: Inventories of services provided by suppliers are maintained
ids.ID.AM-05: Assets are prioritized based on classification, criticality, resources, and impact on the mission
ids.ID.AM-07: Inventories of data and corresponding metadata for designated data types are maintained
ids.ID.AM-08: Systems, hardware, software, services, and data are managed throughout their life cycles
ids.ID.RA-01: Vulnerabilities in assets are identified, validated, and recorded
ids.ID.RA-02: Cyber threat intelligence is received from information sharing forums and sources
ids.ID.RA-03: Internal and external threats to the organization are identified and recorded
ids.ID.RA-04: Potential impacts and likelihoods of threats exploiting vulnerabilities are identified and recorded
ids.ID.RA-05: Threats, vulnerabilities, likelihoods, and impacts are used to understand inherent risk and inform prioritization
ids.ID.RA-06: Risk responses are chosen, prioritized, planned, tracked, and communicated
ids.ID.RA-07: Changes and exceptions are managed, assessed for risk impact, recorded, and tracked
ids.ID.RA-08: Processes for receiving, analyzing, and responding to vulnerability disclosures are established
ids.ID.RA-09: The authenticity and integrity of hardware and software are assessed prior to acquisition and use
ids.ID.RA-10: Critical suppliers are assessed prior to acquisition
ids.ID.IM-02: Improvements are identified from security tests and exercises, including those done with suppliers
ids.ID.IM-03: Improvements are identified from execution of operational processes, procedures, and activities
ids.ID.IM-04: Incident response plans and other cybersecurity plans are established, communicated, maintained, and improved
ids.PR.AA-01: Identities and credentials for authorized users, services, and hardware are managed
ids.PR.AA-02: Identities are proofed and bound to credentials based on the context of interactions
ids.PR.AA-03: Users, services, and hardware are authenticated
ids.PR.AA-04: Identity assertions are protected, conveyed, and verified
ids.PR.AA-05: Access permissions, entitlements, and authorizations are defined in a policy, managed, enforced, and reviewed
ids.PR.AA-06: Physical access to assets is managed, monitored, and enforced commensurate with risk
ids.PR.AT-01: Personnel are provided with awareness and training so that they possess the knowledge and skills to perform general tasks
ids.PR.AT-02: Individuals in specialized roles are provided with awareness and training for their roles
ids.PR.DS-01: The confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data-at-rest are protected
ids.PR.DS-02: The confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data-in-transit are protected
ids.PR.DS-10: The confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data-in-use are protected
ids.PR.DS-11: Backups of data are created, protected, maintained, and tested
ids.PR.PS-01: Configuration management practices are established and applied
ids.PR.PS-02: Software is maintained, replaced, and removed commensurate with risk
ids.PR.PS-03: Hardware is maintained, replaced, and removed commensurate with risk
ids.PR.PS-04: Log records are generated and made available for continuous monitoring
ids.PR.PS-05: Installation and execution of unauthorized software are prevented
ids.PR.PS-06: Secure software development practices are integrated and their performance is monitored
ids.PR.IR-01: Networks and environments are protected from unauthorized logical access and usage
ids.PR.IR-02: The organization's technology assets are protected from environmental threats
ids.PR.IR-03: Mechanisms are implemented to achieve resilience requirements in normal and adverse situations
ids.PR.IR-04: Adequate resource capacity to ensure availability is maintained
ids.DE.CM-01: Networks and network services are monitored to find potentially adverse events
ids.DE.CM-02: The physical environment is monitored to find potentially adverse events
ids.DE.CM-03: Personnel activity and technology usage are monitored to find potentially adverse events
ids.DE.CM-06: External service provider activities and services are monitored to find potentially adverse events
ids.DE.CM-09: Computing hardware and software, runtime environments, and their data are monitored
ids.DE.AE-02: Potentially adverse events are analyzed to better understand associated activities
ids.DE.AE-03: Information is correlated from multiple sources
ids.DE.AE-04: The estimated impact and scope of adverse events are understood
ids.DE.AE-06: Information on adverse events is provided to authorized staff and tools
ids.DE.AE-07: Cyber threat intelligence and other contextual information are integrated into the analysis
ids.DE.AE-08: Incidents are declared when adverse events meet the defined incident criteria
ids.RS.MA-01: The incident response plan is executed in coordination with relevant third parties once an incident is declared
ids.RS.MA-02: Incident reports are triaged and validated
ids.RS.MA-04: Incidents are escalated or elevated as needed
ids.RS.MA-05: The criteria for initiating incident recovery are applied
ids.RS.AN-03: Analysis is performed to establish what has taken place during an incident and the root cause
ids.RS.AN-06: Actions performed during an investigation are recorded, and the records' integrity and provenance are preserved
ids.RS.AN-07: Incident data and metadata are collected, and their integrity and provenance are preserved
ids.RS.AN-08: An incident's magnitude is estimated and validated
ids.RS.CO-02: Internal and external stakeholders are notified of incidents
ids.RS.CO-03: Information is shared with designated internal and external stakeholders
ids.RC.RP-01: The recovery portion of the incident response plan is executed once initiated
ids.RC.RP-02: Recovery actions are selected, scoped, prioritized, and performed
ids.RC.RP-03: The integrity of backups and other restoration assets is verified before use
ids.RC.RP-04: Critical mission functions and cybersecurity risk management are considered to establish post-incident operational norms
ids.RC.RP-05: The integrity of restored assets is verified, systems and services are restored, and normal operating status is confirmed
ids.RC.RP-06: The end of incident recovery is declared based on criteria, and incident-related documentation is completed
ids.RC.CO-03: Recovery activities and progress in restoring operational capabilities are communicated
ids.RC.CO-04: Public updates on incident recovery are shared using approved methods and messaging

cis.name: CIS Critical Security Controls v8.1
cis.plain: A prioritized list of safeguards. Implementation Group 1 (IG1) is the baseline every organization should have; IG2 and IG3 add more.

ids.1.1: Establish and maintain a detailed enterprise asset inventory
ids.2.1: Establish and maintain a software inventory
ids.3.1: Establish and maintain a data management process
ids.3.2: Establish and maintain a data inventory
ids.4.1: Establish and maintain a secure configuration process
ids.5.1: Establish and maintain an inventory of accounts
ids.5.4: Restrict administrator privileges to dedicated administrator accounts
ids.5.5: Establish and maintain an inventory of service accounts
ids.6.3: Require MFA for externally exposed applications
ids.6.4: Require MFA for remote network access
ids.6.8: Define and maintain role-based access control
ids.7.1: Establish and maintain a vulnerability management process
ids.7.2: Establish and maintain a remediation process
ids.7.3: Perform automated operating system patch management
ids.7.5: Perform automated vulnerability scans of internal enterprise assets
ids.8.1: Establish and maintain an audit log management process
ids.11.1: Establish and maintain a data recovery process
ids.11.4: Establish and maintain an isolated instance of recovery data
ids.12.1: Ensure network infrastructure is up to date
ids.14.1: Establish and maintain a security awareness program
ids.14.2: Train workforce members to recognize social engineering attacks
ids.14.6: Train workforce members on recognizing and reporting security incidents
ids.15.1: Establish and maintain an inventory of service providers
ids.15.2: Establish and maintain a service provider management policy
ids.15.4: Ensure service provider contracts include security requirements
ids.16.1: Establish and maintain a secure application development process
ids.16.2: Establish and maintain a process to accept and address software vulnerabilities
ids.16.4: Establish and manage an inventory of third-party software components
ids.16.5: Use up-to-date and trusted third-party software components
ids.16.11: Leverage vetted modules or services for application security components
ids.17.1: Designate personnel to manage incident handling
ids.17.2: Establish and maintain contact information for reporting security incidents
ids.17.3: Establish and maintain an enterprise process for reporting incidents
ids.17.4: Establish and maintain an incident response process
ids.17.6: Define mechanisms for communicating during incident response
ids.18.1: Establish and maintain a penetration testing program

soc2.name: SOC 2 Trust Services Criteria
soc2.plain: The audit report most business customers ask a software vendor for. An outside auditor checks that the vendor's security controls exist and worked over a period of time.

ids.CC1.1: COSO Principle 1: commitment to integrity and ethical values
ids.CC1.2: COSO Principle 2: board independence and oversight
ids.CC1.3: COSO Principle 3: structures, reporting lines, authorities, and responsibilities
ids.CC1.4: COSO Principle 4: commitment to attract, develop, and retain competent individuals
ids.CC1.5: COSO Principle 5: individuals held accountable for internal control responsibilities
ids.CC2.1: Relevant, quality information is used to support internal control
ids.CC2.2: Internal communication of information, including objectives and responsibilities
ids.CC2.3: External communication regarding matters affecting internal control
ids.CC3.1: Objectives specified with sufficient clarity to identify and assess risks
ids.CC3.2: Risks to objectives identified and analyzed as a basis for managing them
ids.CC3.3: Potential for fraud considered in assessing risks
ids.CC3.4: Changes that could significantly affect internal control are identified and assessed
ids.CC4.1: Ongoing and separate evaluations to ascertain whether controls are present and functioning
ids.CC4.2: Internal control deficiencies evaluated and communicated in a timely manner
ids.CC5.1: Control activities selected and developed to mitigate risks
ids.CC5.2: General control activities over technology selected and developed
ids.CC5.3: Control activities deployed through policies and procedures
ids.CC6.1: Logical access security software, infrastructure, and architectures over protected information assets
ids.CC6.2: Registration and authorization of new users; credentials removed when access is no longer authorized
ids.CC6.3: Access to data, software, functions, and other protected assets authorized, modified, or removed based on roles and least privilege
ids.CC6.4: Physical access to facilities and protected information assets restricted
ids.CC6.5: Logical and physical protections over physical assets discontinued only after data is diminished
ids.CC6.6: Logical access security measures against threats from sources outside system boundaries
ids.CC6.7: Transmission, movement, and removal of information restricted to authorized users and processes; protected in transit
ids.CC6.8: Controls to prevent or detect and act upon unauthorized or malicious software
ids.CC7.1: Detection and monitoring procedures to identify configuration changes and new vulnerabilities
ids.CC7.2: System components monitored for anomalies indicative of malicious acts, natural disasters, and errors
ids.CC7.3: Security events evaluated to determine whether they could or have resulted in a failure to meet objectives
ids.CC7.4: Response to identified security incidents through an incident response program
ids.CC8.1: Changes to infrastructure, data, software, and procedures authorized, designed, developed, tested, approved, and implemented
ids.CC9.1: Risk mitigation activities for business disruptions
ids.CC9.2: Vendor and business partner risks assessed and managed
ids.A1.1: Current processing capacity and use of system components maintained, monitored, and evaluated
ids.A1.2: Environmental protections, software, data backup processes, and recovery infrastructure implemented
ids.C1.2: Confidential information disposed of to meet objectives

airmf.name: NIST AI Risk Management Framework 1.0
airmf.version: 1.0 (January 2023) with the Generative AI Profile (NIST AI 600-1, July 2024)
airmf.plain: The US government's voluntary guide for managing AI risk. Four parts: Govern (who is accountable), Map (what the system does and who it affects), Measure (test it), Manage (act on what you find). Compliance with it is an affirmative defense under the Texas AI law.

ids.GOVERN 1.1: Legal and regulatory requirements involving AI are understood, managed, and documented
ids.GOVERN 1.2: Trustworthy AI characteristics are integrated into organizational policies, processes, and practices
ids.GOVERN 1.3: Processes and procedures determine the needed level of risk management activities based on risk tolerance
ids.GOVERN 1.4: Risk management process and its outcomes are established through transparent policies and procedures
ids.GOVERN 1.5: Ongoing monitoring and periodic review of the risk management process and its outcomes are planned
ids.GOVERN 1.6: Mechanisms are in place to inventory AI systems and are resourced according to risk priorities
ids.GOVERN 1.7: Processes and procedures are in place for decommissioning and phasing out AI systems safely
ids.GOVERN 2.1: Roles and responsibilities and lines of communication related to mapping, measuring, and managing AI risks are documented
ids.GOVERN 2.2: The organization's personnel and partners receive AI risk management training
ids.GOVERN 2.3: Executive leadership takes responsibility for decisions about risks associated with AI system development and deployment
ids.GOVERN 3.2: Policies and procedures define and differentiate roles and responsibilities for human-AI configurations and oversight
ids.GOVERN 4.1: Organizational policies and practices foster a critical thinking and safety-first mindset
ids.GOVERN 4.2: Organizational teams document the risks and potential impacts of the AI technology they design, develop, deploy, or use
ids.GOVERN 4.3: Organizational practices are in place to enable AI testing, identification of incidents, and information sharing
ids.GOVERN 5.1: Organizational policies and practices collect, consider, prioritize, and integrate feedback from external stakeholders
ids.GOVERN 6.1: Policies and procedures address AI risks associated with third-party software and data
ids.GOVERN 6.2: Contingency processes handle failures or incidents in third-party data or AI systems deemed high-risk
ids.MAP 1.1: Intended purposes, potentially beneficial uses, context-specific laws, norms and expectations, and settings are understood and documented
ids.MAP 1.2: Interdisciplinary AI actors, competencies, skills, and capacities for establishing context are prioritized
ids.MAP 1.5: Organizational risk tolerances are determined and documented
ids.MAP 2.1: The specific tasks and methods used to implement the tasks that the AI system will support are defined
ids.MAP 2.2: Information about the AI system's knowledge limits and how system output may be utilized and overseen by humans is documented
ids.MAP 3.4: Processes for operator and practitioner proficiency with AI system performance and trustworthiness are defined
ids.MAP 4.1: Approaches for mapping AI technology and legal risks of its components, including third-party data or software, are in place
ids.MAP 5.1: Likelihood and magnitude of each identified impact are identified and documented
ids.MEASURE 1.1: Approaches and metrics for measurement of AI risks are selected for implementation
ids.MEASURE 1.3: Internal experts who did not serve as front-line developers and independent assessors are involved in assessments
ids.MEASURE 2.5: The AI system to be deployed is demonstrated to be valid and reliable
ids.MEASURE 2.6: The AI system is evaluated regularly for safety risks
ids.MEASURE 2.7: AI system security and resilience are evaluated and documented
ids.MEASURE 2.8: Risks associated with transparency and accountability are examined and documented
ids.MEASURE 2.9: The AI model is explained, validated, and documented
ids.MEASURE 2.10: Privacy risk of the AI system is examined and documented
ids.MEASURE 3.1: Approaches, personnel, and documentation are in place to regularly identify and track existing, unanticipated, and emergent AI risks
ids.MEASURE 3.3: Feedback processes for end users and impacted communities to report problems are established
ids.MEASURE 4.2: Measurement results regarding AI system trustworthiness in deployment context are informed by input from domain experts
ids.MANAGE 1.1: A determination is made as to whether the AI system achieves its intended purposes
ids.MANAGE 1.3: Responses to the AI risks deemed high priority are developed, planned, and documented
ids.MANAGE 2.2: Mechanisms are in place and applied to sustain the value of deployed AI systems
ids.MANAGE 2.3: Procedures are followed to respond to and recover from a previously unknown risk when it is identified
ids.MANAGE 2.4: Mechanisms are in place and applied to supersede, disengage, or deactivate AI systems that demonstrate performance inconsistent with intended use
ids.MANAGE 3.1: AI risks and benefits from third-party resources are regularly monitored, and risk controls are applied and documented
ids.MANAGE 3.2: Pre-trained models which are used for development are monitored as part of AI system regular monitoring and maintenance
ids.MANAGE 4.1: Post-deployment AI system monitoring plans are implemented, including mechanisms for capturing and evaluating input from users
ids.MANAGE 4.2: Measurable activities for continual improvements are integrated into AI system updates
ids.MANAGE 4.3: Incidents and errors are communicated to relevant AI actors, including affected communities

soc2_report.name: SOC 2 Type II report
soc2_report.plain: Customers ask for this audit report before they buy. Nimbus holds one (simulated).

sb2610.name: Texas SB 2610 cybersecurity safe harbor
sb2610.plain: A Texas law (effective September 1, 2025). A business under 250 employees that adopts and maintains a recognized security framework cannot be hit with exemplary damages after a breach. At 100 to 249 employees the qualifying frameworks include NIST CSF and ISO/IEC 27001.

traiga.name: Texas Responsible AI Governance Act (HB 149)
traiga.plain: A Texas AI law (effective January 1, 2026) that applies to companies deploying AI in Texas. Following the NIST AI Risk Management Framework is an affirmative defense; the Attorney General enforces it with a 60-day cure period.

tx_breach.name: Texas breach notification (Bus. and Com. Code 521.053)
tx_breach.plain: After a breach of sensitive personal information, affected people must be told within 60 days, and the Attorney General within 30 days when 250 or more Texas residents are affected.

pci_saq_a.name: PCI DSS v4.0.1 SAQ A
pci_saq_a.plain: Card payments are handled by a payment processor; card numbers never touch Nimbus systems, so the lightest PCI self-assessment applies.

gdpr.name: GDPR (EU customers)
gdpr.plain: Nimbus has customers in the EU, so it acts as a data processor for their personal data and must meet EU privacy rules.

hipaa_baa.name: HIPAA business associate agreements (Enterprise add-on)
hipaa_baa.plain: Enterprise customers in healthcare can sign a business associate agreement, which brings HIPAA Security Rule duties for their data.

eu_ai_act.name: EU AI Act
eu_ai_act.plain: EU rules for AI. Customer-facing chat assistants are limited-risk systems that must tell people they are talking to AI (Article 50, applies from August 2, 2026). High-risk obligations were deferred to December 2, 2027 by the 2026 Digital Omnibus.
